clue.text: Fate of cracked Meissen?

indicators.note: porcelain that is cracked is broken up, so the letters of the china's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: What becomes of a piece of fine German porcelain once it is cracked?
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' turns MEISSEN into the new order. Meissen is a German porcelain maker, so the surface is about broken china.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis is an inescapable agent of downfall, one's destined doom, so it serves for fate.

clue.text: Mother-of-pearl from northern area

parts.note: an acre is a unit of land area

explanation.surface: A source of mother-of-pearl found in some northern region.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is the iridescent lining of shells, the substance also called mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: Cissy gets benefit from work

parts.note: to milk something is to exploit it for gain
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A weakling profits from somebody else's labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a feeble, timid man, the same insult as a cissy.

clue.text: Like valuations of 4?

parts.note: the ratings of the agency at 4 down are read literally as 'standard and poor', which describes something mediocre

explanation.surface: A question about the kind of ratings a credit agency gives.
explanation.walkthrough: The agency at 4 down is Standard and Poor's; take its name as a verdict, 'standard and poor', and you have a two-word phrase for middling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only standard and poor is middling or mediocre, the meaning of this reduplicated phrase.

clue.text: Are their ratings never very good?

definitions.text: Are their ratings never very good?

parts.words: Are their ratings never very good?
parts.note: the credit agency's name, read as plain words, says its marks are merely average and weak

explanation.surface: A dig at a credit-rating agency, asking whether it ever gives a top mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Standard and Poor's is a US credit-rating agency; its name read as two adjectives suggests its ratings are never very good.
explanation.definitionFit: The agency named here issues credit ratings, and its name literally pairs two words for mediocre.

clue.text: Recall astonishing miracle

indicators.note: something astonishing knocks things sideways, so the word miracle is jumbled

explanation.surface: Remembering an amazing miracle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recall' looks like 'remember' in the surface; here it means call back, as a manufacturer recalls faulty goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall goods or land is to demand them back, which is to take possession again.

clue.text: Gamble like Putin allowed to get in the way

parts.note: Vladimir Putin is Russian

indicators.note: one piece is told to enter the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: a route is the way taken
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A wager in the Putin style, permitted to stand in someone's path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get in' signals the container. 'like Putin' reads as a comparison but simply means Russian, Putin being Russia's president.
explanation.definitionFit: The deadly game with a revolver is the ultimate reckless gamble, and the phrase means any dangerous risk.

clue.text: Seize and study its face change

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: the instruction to change tells us to rearrange the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Grab something, look at it closely, and alter its appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges 'its face'. CON as 'study' is an old verb, as in conning one's lines; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To confiscate is to take property by authority, a formal way of seizing it.

clue.text: Not quite 13 together with advance payment

parts.note: and joins things, meaning together with
an ante is a stake paid in before play in poker

explanation.surface: Almost at a crawl, plus a deposit paid up front.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 down is a very slow speed; the musical tempo meant here is slow but walking pace, so 'not quite' that slow.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a moderately slow musical tempo, a walking pace, quicker than a crawl.

clue.text: Evergreens — if failing, try elms

indicators.note: if the attempt with elms is failing, the letters of those words are reworked

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: if your evergreens die, plant elms instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' turns TRYELMS into the answer's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtles are aromatic shrubs that keep their glossy leaves all year round.

clue.text: Weather conditions bringing infections need kips

parts.note: colds are viral infections
kip is British slang for sleep, so kips are short sleeps

explanation.surface: Wintry weather gives people colds and they need more sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold snaps are sudden short spells of freezing weather.

clue.text: Drain off to the bottom

indicators.note: off suggests the word drain has gone wrong, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Run the water off down to the very bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns DRAIN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, literally the point below an observer.

clue.text: Egghead goes to one college or other …

indicators.note: the head of the word egg is its first letter

parts.note: the LSE is the London School of Economics, a college of London University

explanation.surface: A brainy type heads off to a university college or somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like one word for an intellectual; split it, the head of 'Egg' gives E. The ellipsis runs the sentence on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Else and other are synonyms, as in 'someone else' meaning some other person.

clue.text: … as well as a bit of maths with a student

definitions.note: a phrase meaning in addition, standing for the adjective extra

parts.note: addition is one of the basic operations of arithmetic
L for learner, as on the plates of a learner driver

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: one bright pupil also studies sums alongside another learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional is extra, added on as well as what was already there.

clue.text: Tacks away from earth with little motion

annotationWithheld.why: Tacks away from earth with little motion (6,4): NAILS (tacks) + SPACE (away from earth) gives NAILSSPACE, not SNAILSPACE; the only fix makes 'away' both an anagram indicator for NAILS and part of SPACE, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Tacks away from earth with little motion

clue.text: Starter key

definitions.meaning: the first course of a meal, or the opening item
a key opens a lock, as does a tin or bottle ...

explanation.definitionFit: An opener is both the thing that begins proceedings and a tool that unlocks or opens something.

clue.text: Centre of 16 across following Dutch uncle

indicators.note: following says the country comes after the scrambled relative
Dutch is used here to mean the uncle is scrambled, as foreign double-Dutch is garbled

parts.note: the country at 16 across is abbreviated US

explanation.surface: Sounds like a strict lecture at the heart of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' turns UNCLE into NUCLE; a Dutch uncle is someone who gives blunt advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the central core around which other parts gather.

clue.text: Country morning with Heath

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means morning
erica is the botanical genus of heath plants

explanation.surface: A countryside scene of morning on the heath, or a nod to a British prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heath' with its capital suggests Edward Heath, the British prime minister; it is the plant heath, genus Erica.
explanation.definitionFit: America is a country, commonly naming the United States.

clue.text: Jar of current and classic time

parts.note: an amp is a unit of electric current
hora is the classical Latin word for an hour

explanation.surface: A vessel holding electricity from ancient times.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a two-handled ancient Greek or Roman storage jar.

clue.text: Times create articles of crap

annotationWithheld.why: Times create articles of crap (7): X (times) + CREATE rearranged gives the letters, but no word signals the anagram; 'articles of' would have to be the indicator, or the definition 'articles of crap' leaves the anagram unsignalled

clue.text: Nothing to bone of bones

parts.note: O, the round zero, means nothing
bone is slang for steal

explanation.surface: Zero to gnaw on, just a bone made of bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bone' looks anatomical beside the definition, but it is the slang verb meaning to pinch.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteal is the adjective meaning relating to bone or bony tissue.

clue.text: This sale is indeed smart

indicators.note: in, split off the start of indeed, places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a deed is an action
U means upper-class, posh or smart

explanation.surface: A claim that this sale is truly stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' splits into 'in deed': U goes in ACTION. U as upper-class is old British slang for socially smart.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a public sale where goods go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Carried by beasts, parcels can go off

parts.note: packs are parcels or bundles
eggs that addle go bad, that is go off

explanation.surface: Beasts of burden carry parcels that can be dropped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' reads as leaving; it means to rot, as eggs addle.
explanation.definitionFit: A packsaddle is the saddle a pack animal wears, so it is borne by beasts.

clue.text: Book cast out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of cast are put out of order

explanation.surface: A book thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns CAST into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acts of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Some considerable number took part in battle

indicators.note: the large number joins in by going inside the word some

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number

explanation.surface: A good many people fought in the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took part in' puts M inside SOME. The Somme was a major First World War battle in 1916.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme is the 1916 battle fought along the French river of that name.

clue.text: Settlement for Peterhouse, initially by the river

indicators.note: by means next to, so the initial letter sits beside the river

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of Peterhouse

explanation.surface: A place to live for a Cambridge college, beside its river.
explanation.walkthrough: Peterhouse is the oldest Cambridge college, which stands by the Cam.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp is a temporary settlement of tents or huts.

clue.text: Letter gives a sign of resistance

definitions.meaning: the last letter of the Greek alphabet
the symbol for the ohm, the unit of electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A letter is the symbol of defiance.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is both the final Greek letter and the symbol used for ohms in electronics.

clue.text: It's exclusive East European xenophobia

parts.note: Ost is German for east
racism is hostility to people of other races, like fear of foreigners

explanation.surface: Fear of outsiders in Eastern Europe is a closed affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostracism shuts people out of a group, so it is by nature excluding.

clue.text: A buddy rejects sport for which he's not paid

parts.note: a mate is a friend or buddy

indicators.note: rejects turns the sport back on itself, so it is read backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A friend turns down a game that he plays for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejects' turns RU into UR at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur takes part for love rather than payment, unlike a professional.

clue.text: Stretch of river carrying vessels

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A stretch of river with boats on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' suggests boats on the river; they are pans held inside EXE.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide stretch of open land, water or sky.
